sentence: To find a nonzero polynomial \( P(x, y) \) such that \( P(\lfloor a \rfloor, \lfloor 2a \rfloor) = 0 \) for all real numbers \( a \), we start by analyzing the relationship between \( \lfloor a \rfloor \) and \( \lfloor 2a \rfloor \).
sentence-category-reason: Restates the goal and outlines the next step to analyze the relationship.

sentence: For any real number \( a \), let \( a = n + f \) where \( n \) is an integer and \( 0 \leq f < 1 \).
sentence-category-reason: Introduces notation by decomposing a into integer and fractional parts.
Deduces a direct relationship from the introduced notation.

sentence: The value \( 2a = 2n + 2f \), so \( \lfloor 2a \rfloor \) is either \( 2n \) if \( 0 \leq f < 0.5 \) or \( 2n + 1 \) if \( 0.5 \leq f < 1 \).
sentence-category-reason: Carries out computation and case analysis for floor(2a).

sentence: Therefore, \( \lfloor 2a \rfloor \) can be either \( 2 \lfloor a \rfloor \) or \( 2 \lfloor a \rfloor + 1 \).
sentence-category-reason: Concludes a general relationship between the floors from prior steps.

sentence: This means for any integer \( x = \lfloor a \rfloor \), the corresponding \( y = \lfloor 2a \rfloor \) must be either \( 2x \) or \( 2x + 1 \).
sentence-category-reason: Restates the derived relationship in terms of x and y.

sentence: A polynomial that vanishes when \( y \) is either \( 2x \) or \( 2x + 1 \) can be constructed by taking the product of the factors \( (y - 2x) \) and \( (y - 2x - 1) \).
sentence-category-reason: Proposes the construction method for a polynomial via chosen factors.

sentence: This product will be zero whenever \( y \) is \( 2x \) or \( 2x + 1 \).
sentence-category-reason: Explains why the constructed product vanishes in the required cases.

sentence: Thus, the polynomial \( P(x, y) = (y - 2x)(y - 2x - 1) \) satisfies the condition for all real numbers \( a \).
sentence-category-reason: Concludes that the constructed polynomial satisfies the problem’s condition.
